questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

A government is planning to intervene in a free market to fix output at the level that maximises the economic welfare of society. MSC = MPC costs, benefits Y T X S MSB MPB O W R output To achieve its objective, what should the government introduce?

options.A: a subsidy of TS
options.B: a subsidy of YX

questions.questionText: In a two-person economy, X has an income of $100, whereas Y has an income of $50. According to the Pareto criterion, which income change would constitute a definite increase in the economic welfare? X’s income Y’s income ($) ($)

The diagram shows three budget lines, QR, QT and SR. QR is a consumer’s initial budget line. good Y Q S O R T good X Which combination of changes could cause the budget line to shift to SR? price of consumer’s good X income

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase

questions.questionText: When a firm increases all its inputs by 100%, its output increases by 50%. What does this illustrate?

options.A: decreasing returns to scale
options.B: economies of scale

questions.questionText: The demand curve for a good has unit price elasticity throughout its length. Which statement about marginal revenue is correct?

options.A: It always has a negative value.
options.B: It decreases continuously as price decreases.
options.D: It always has a constant positive value.

questions.questionText: What is true about the average fixed costs of a firm?

options.A: They fall as output rises at first, but then rise.
options.B: They fall continuously as output rises.
options.C: They increase continuously as output rises.
options.D: They remain unchanged at all output levels.

questions.questionText: In the diagram MC = marginal cost; AC = average cost; MR = marginal revenue; AR = average revenue. MC MR cost, revenue AC AR O W X Y Z output What will be the output of a profit-maximising firm whose cost and revenue functions are shown above?

options.A: OW B OX C OY D OZ

options.A: marginal revenue is equal to marginal cost.
options.B: average revenue is equal to average cost.
options.C: marginal revenue is equal to average revenue.

Firms in a market advertise their products with different brand names. Some make more profit than others in the short run but all make normal profit in the long run. Which market structure is this?

options.A: perfect competition
options.B: monopolistic competition

questions.questionText: Which feature of an oligopoly can be explained by the kinked demand curve model?

options.A: collusion between firms in the determination of the industry price
options.B: price leadership by one firm in the industry
options.C: the ability of firms to earn abnormal profits in the long run
options.D: the reluctance of firms to alter prices

OS system GB 2012 (%) GB 2015 (%) US 2012 (%) US 2015 (%) V 49.3 54.3 43.0 65.6 W 15.7 1.0 3.3 0.4 X 29.3 32.7 50.6 30.1 Y 2.4 12.0 2.1 3.8 Z 3.3 0.0 1.0 0.1 What can be concluded from the table about changes between 2012 and 2015?

options.A: The dominant firm in each country increased its market power.
options.B: The firms counted in the three-firm concentration ratio remained the same in both countries.
options.C: The three-firm concentration ratio decreased in both countries.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a Lorenz curve, with two areas, X and Y, identified. cumulative line of % of income perfect equality X Y Lorenz curve cumulative % of households How is the corresponding Gini coefficient calculated?

options.A: X divided by (X plus Y)
options.B: X plus Y divided by X

questions.questionText: The government of a country wants to achieve a more equitable distribution of income. Which combination of measures is likely to be most effective in achieving this aim? tax-free income allowance welfare benefits

options.A: decrease reduce means-tested benefits
options.B: decrease reduce universal benefits

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper earns $75 per week, but he would be willing to carry on working in his shop for up to $25 per week less. Therefore, $50 is his level of

options.A: marginal revenue product.
options.B: producer’s surplus.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the supply and demand for labour in an industry. S wage rate W D O L M N employment Initially the industry’s labour market is in equilibrium. What effect will the introduction of a minimum wage OW have on the level of employment in the industry?

options.A: It will decrease by LM.
options.B: It will decrease by LN.

questions.questionText: Immigrants are awarded entry points according to their ability to fulfil criteria set by the Canadian Government. A new Express Entry system for the immigration of skilled workers was introduced. The diagram shows the change in the relative importance or weighting given to these criteria between the old and new systems. Criteria weighting (%) for skilled worker immigration skill transferability work experience % adaptability 80 age education language job offer old Express system Entry system What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: Canada intended to maintain the same level of skilled immigrants under both systems.
options.B: Canada wanted a smaller number of highly educated skilled immigrants.
options.C: Certainty of employment for skilled immigrants was made the main criterion.
options.D: Skilled immigrants needed to have fewer years of work experience than previously.

questions.questionText: It has been observed that increased growth in consumer spending results in an increase in investment by firms. Which principle of macroeconomic theory explains this relationship?

options.A: the accelerator
options.B: the liquidity trap

How do commercial banks create money?

options.A: by cashing cheques for their customers
options.B: by increasing their reserves at the central bank
options.D: by charging customers for banking services

questions.questionText: What are the variables identified on the axes of a Kuznets curve diagram? vertical (Y) axis variable horizontal (X) axis variable

options.A: cumulative % of income cumulative % of families
options.B: measure of inequality income per capita
options.C: measure of standard of living economic growth rate

questions.questionText: A developing country experiences economic growth. The economic growth is most likely to lead to economic development when it

options.A: causes rapid rural to urban migration.
options.B: is based on the extraction of mineral raw materials.
options.D: results from the expansion of labour-intensive industries.

questions.questionText: Between 2014 and 2015 the Polish economy expanded at a rate of 3.3%. What necessarily follows from this statement?

options.A: The cost of living rose by 3.3%.
options.B: The output of the industrial sector rose by 3.3%.
options.C: There was increased demand which caused inflation.

What will result in the short run from rising unemployment in an economy?

options.A: The government’s budget deficit will fall.
options.B: Any existing inflationary pressure will be reduced.
options.D: The economy’s production possibility curve will move inwards.

questions.questionText: In 2015 a political party proposed a policy of quantitative easing (the creation of money by the central bank). When would such a policy be least likely to destabilise the macro economy in the short run?

options.A: when the economy was experiencing a high level of inflation
options.B: when the economy had price stability but there was full employment of the labour force
options.C: when there existed a deep recession with high levels of unemployment
options.D: when there was full employment and a current account balance of payments deficit

questions.questionText: In 1979 in the UK the marginal rate of income tax imposed on the highest earners was 83% which increased to 98% if income was received from interest or dividends. By 1989 the highest marginal rate was reduced to 40%. Despite this reduction, the tax revenue raised from the highest earners increased substantially. Which theoretical concept illustrates this relationship between tax rates and tax revenue?

options.A: the J curve
options.B: the Laffer curve

questions.questionText: Which factor has been least associated with the rapid growth of many economies recently?

options.A: high savings rates as a percentage of national income
options.B: more efficient mechanisms for transmitting funds from savers to investors
options.C: more emphasis on detailed government planning
